# circuit-breaker

Circuit breaker resilience primitive for PHP. `Closed → Open → HalfOpen`
state, switched by sliding-window success/failure counts, via a shared
in-memory, APCu, or Redis `Storage`.

Install:

```
composer require rasuvaeff/circuit-breaker
```

Runtime deps: `rasuvaeff/duration`, `psr/clock`. For `RedisStorage`
(multi-host) also install ONE Redis client — `predis/predis` ^2.2 (pure-PHP,
`PredisScriptRunner`) or `ext-redis` (`PhpRedisScriptRunner`); both optional
(`suggest`). `ext-apcu` for `ApcuStorage` (single-host) — also optional.
Namespace `Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker`.

## Rules

- PHP 8.3+, `declare(strict_types=1)`, immutable `final readonly` classes.
- `isFailure` is required in `BreakerConfig`; classify only exceptions that
  indicate a downstream failure (network errors, 5xx status).
- `classifyResult` is optional and defaults to `Outcome::Success`. Use it for
  normal API responses that represent downstream failure; the original result
  is still returned and fallback is not invoked.
- `CircuitObserver` receives committed `CircuitTransition` events after storage
  commit; configure its paired error handler to isolate telemetry failures.
- `Ratio::of(failures, window, within)`: a ring buffer capped at `window`
  entries, pruned to the last `within` duration. Opens when the failure count
  within that buffer reaches `failures`.
- In `Open`, `call()` never invokes the callback — it throws
  `CircuitOpenException` (or calls `fallback` with it) instantly.
- `fallback` is invoked on `Rejected` (with a fresh `CircuitOpenException`) OR
  when the callback threw and `isFailure()` classified it as `Failure`. An
  `Ignored` outcome (`isFailure() === false`) is ALWAYS rethrown as-is, never
  triggers `fallback`, never counts against the threshold.
- `probeLimit` (default 1) bounds concurrent probes admitted in `HalfOpen`;
  `successThreshold` consecutive probe successes close the circuit again; any
  probe failure reopens immediately and restarts the cooldown clock.
- `probeTimeout` (default `cooldown`) leases HalfOpen probe slots and reclaims
  abandoned slots after the timeout. `CircuitBreaker::call()` passes an opaque
  attempt ID so a reclaimed probe cannot affect a newer Redis generation.
- Outcomes are timestamped when the callback completes. Storage exceptions
  become `StorageFailure` infrastructure errors; they are never classified by
  `isFailure` and never trigger `fallback`. Inspect `operation` and
  `getPrevious()` for logging/degradation.
- `name` must match `/^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$/` (it becomes part of the Redis/APCu key).
- `InMemoryStorage` is single-process only (tests/CLI) — not cross-process.
- `ApcuStorage` only coordinates workers on the same host — use `RedisStorage`
  across hosts. Lock-budget exhaustion throws; through `CircuitBreaker` it is
  exposed as `StorageFailure`, never as a silently lost transition. Its lock is
  a LEASE (`lockTtlSeconds`, default 1s), not a mutex: a critical section that
  outlives the lease fails the commit instead of overwriting another worker's
  write. A failed `apcu_store()` (segment full) throws for the same reason.
- `RedisStorage` runs `admit()`/`recordOutcome()`/`snapshot()`/`forceState()`
  each as ONE atomic Lua script (EVALSHA with EVAL fallback on NOSCRIPT) — this
  is what makes the read-evaluate-transition sequence race-free across
  processes. Implement `CircuitScriptRunner` to back it with another client.
- `snapshot()`/`state()`/`metrics()` never mutate — they don't apply the lazy
  `Open → HalfOpen` cooldown transition or prune the window. Only `call()`
  (via `admit()`/`recordOutcome()`) does.
- `RedisStorage` uses Redis server time by default for cooldown and probe leases.
  `useServerTime: false` is a deterministic caller-clock mode for tests; APCu
  always uses the injected clock, so distributed APCu users need NTP.
- Redis probe fencing is strict in both time modes: an opaque attempt ID is
  stored in the active probe set and removed or invalidated atomically.
- This package does not retry or limit concurrency — compose with
  `rasuvaeff/retry` and `rasuvaeff/bulkhead`.

`Storage::admit()` returns `AdmissionResult`; `recordOutcome()` returns
`OutcomeResult`. Both expose optional transition metadata: a committed
`CircuitTransition` carries a `TransitionReason`
(`failure-threshold-reached`, `cooldown-elapsed`, `probe-succeeded`,
`probe-failed`, `forced-open`, `forced-closed`, `forced-half-open`).
`StorageOperation` enumerates storage operation names used in infrastructure
error routing.

## API

```php
use Psr\Http\Client\ClientExceptionInterface;
use Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker\BreakerConfig;
use Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker\CircuitBreaker;
use Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker\Clock\SystemClock;
use Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker\InMemoryStorage;
use Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker\Ratio;
use Rasuvaeff\Duration\Duration;

$cb = new CircuitBreaker(
    config: new BreakerConfig(
        name: 'stripe',
        failureThreshold: Ratio::of(failures: 5, window: 10, within: Duration::seconds(60)),
        cooldown: Duration::seconds(30),
        successThreshold: 3,
        probeLimit: 1,
        isFailure: static fn(\Throwable $e): bool => $e instanceof ClientExceptionInterface,
    ),
    storage: new InMemoryStorage(), // or ApcuStorage / RedisStorage
    clock: new SystemClock(),
);

$result = $cb->call(
    callback: static fn(): mixed => callDownstream(),
    fallback: static fn(\Throwable $e): mixed => degradedResult(),
);

$cb->canCall();   // bool, best-effort, side-effect-free
$cb->state();     // CircuitState::Closed|Open|HalfOpen
$cb->metrics();   // Metrics: state(), successes(), failures(), rejected(), openedAt()
$cb->forceOpen();
$cb->forceClosed();
```

With Redis (multi-host):

```php
use Predis\Client;
use Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker\Redis\PredisScriptRunner;
use Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker\RedisStorage;

$storage = new RedisStorage(new PredisScriptRunner(new Client(['host' => '127.0.0.1'])));
```

With `ext-redis` instead of predis:

```php
use Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker\Redis\PhpRedisScriptRunner;

$redis = new \Redis();
$redis->connect('127.0.0.1');
$storage = new RedisStorage(new PhpRedisScriptRunner($redis));
```

Single-host, no Redis:

```php
use Rasuvaeff\CircuitBreaker\ApcuStorage;

$storage = new ApcuStorage(); // ApcuStorage::isAvailable() to check ext-apcu
```

### Storage (implement for a custom backend)

```php
interface Storage
{
    public function admit(string $key, BreakerConfig $config, \DateTimeImmutable $now, string $attemptId): AdmissionResult;
    public function recordOutcome(string $key, Outcome $outcome, BreakerConfig $config, \DateTimeImmutable $now, Admission $admission, \DateTimeImmutable $admittedAt, string $attemptId): OutcomeResult;
    public function snapshot(string $key): StateRecord;      // read-only, no side effects
    public function forceState(string $key, CircuitState $state, \DateTimeImmutable $now): ?CircuitTransition;
}
```

`admit()`/`recordOutcome()` MUST be one atomic operation each — read state,
evaluate thresholds, transition — not a sequence of smaller primitives (that
reopens a check-then-act race between processes).

The fencing triple (`$admission`, `$admittedAt`, `$attemptId`) is REQUIRED, not
optional: pass back exactly what `admit()` was called with, one
`recordOutcome()` per admission. Fabricating it defeats probe fencing — Redis
matches `$attemptId` against the live probe set, the PHP-side backends compare
`$admittedAt` against the current probe generation.

An outcome whose admission is not `Admission::Probe` never moves a `HalfOpen`
breaker: it was admitted while the breaker was still `Closed`, so it belongs to
no probe generation.

### Composition (rasuvaeff/retry, rasuvaeff/bulkhead — not dependencies)

```php
// retry inside one call, breaker blocks after a systemic outage
$cb->call(fn () => $retry->run(fn () => callDownstream()));

// bulkhead limits parallelism, breaker blocks cascading failure
$bulkhead->call(fn () => $cb->call(fn () => callDownstream()));
```
